messages:
ken-customer: Hey team — customer hitting repeated 503s when calling our hosted API over their PrivateLink endpoint. Started after they flipped to the interface endpoint. Errors only for some requests, intermittently.

elaine-support: Sorry to hear that — can you paste the full repro steps and any client-side logs? is this only from one VPC?

ken-customer: Repro steps: 1) create interface endpoint to com.amazonaws.vpce.my-region.vpce-svc-abc (our service) 2) resolve api.redwood.internal -> 10.5.12.34 (endpoint ENI) 3) curl https://api.redwood.internal/v1/complete -> sometimes 503, sometimes 200. No changes to security groups. Happens from multiple subnets in their VPC.

elaine-support: do we have LB / target group health status for their tenant? raj, can you pull target health for the NLB target group serving that account?

raj-infra: pulled it — target group shows intermittent Unhealthy state toggling. Health checks from the NLB are failing ~10% of checks. Target type is "instance" (not IP). Important detail: when traffic comes via VPCE, source IPs seen by the backend are the ENI IPs from the interface endpoint service, not the original client. If backend firewall or host-based ACLs expect original client IPs, health checks/handshake might be blocked.

sasha-eng: also saw TLS handshakes failing in some of the captured logs. When we replicate against the target IP directly (bypassing endpoint DNS), openssl s_client shows a certificate CN mismatch occasionally. My suspicion: some clients/health probes are connecting by IP (no SNI) so the backend presents default cert -> backend rejects or app returns 503.

ken-customer: how are probes coming from NLB vs VPCE? we didn't touch any app certs.

raj-infra: quick breakdown: - Client -> VPCE ENI (10.x) -> AWS PrivateLink forwards to service NLB -> NLB forwards to registered targets. Health checks originate from the load balancer to targets; connection path differs depending on target type. If the target group is instance-based and the app does SNI-based routing (virtual hosts), connection by IP (no SNI) can hit default vhost. Also, if security group on targets only allows specific source IP ranges (expecting client IPs), it can intermittently block when source is the endpoint ENI.

elaine-support: can you reproduce with curl + openssl? please include exact commands so we can hand back to customer.

sasha-eng: repro commands I used:
```
# resolve endpoint ENI IP
dig +short api.redwood.internal @10.5.12.2
# curl with SNI/Host header
curl -v --resolve api.redwood.internal:443:10.5.12.34 https://api.redwood.internal/health
# openssl to inspect certs (SNI)
openssl s_client -connect 10.5.12.34:443 -servername api.redwood.internal
# openssl without SNI shows default cert
openssl s_client -connect 10.5.12.34:443
```

sasha-eng: results: with -servername we get correct cert (CN=api.redwood.internal) and 200. Without -servername we see default cert and 503 from the app.

ken-customer: we don't explicitly set Host in some of our SDK calls (we rely on DNS). Could VPCE be stripping SNI?

raj-infra: VPCE does not strip SNI by default. But some proxies or middleboxes in their VPC (transparent proxies, egress NAT devices) can terminate TLS or do TLS-inspection and re-initiate TLS without SNI preserved. Also check if client is using HTTP/1.0 fallback or older TLS stack that doesn't send SNI.

elaine-support: action items for customer (quick checklist):
- Ensure clients set Host and send SNI (modern SDKs do this). Provide the two curl commands above.
- Confirm there's no TLS-terminating proxy on the client path (check VPC route table for explicit proxy or Transit Gateway appliances).
- Check security group on app instances allows inbound from the VPCE ENI CIDR (the endpoint interface ENIs).
- If target group type is instance, consider switching to IP target type so original source translation is preserved as expected for your topology.

raj-infra: additional infra checks we did for them:
- Verified NLB listener is TCP/TLS passthrough (we prefer TLS passthrough to preserve SNI to backend)
- Confirmed health check path /health accepts Host header and returns 200 when Host present
- Noted NACLs were OK. However the customer's app-level firewall had a CIDR allowlist that didn't include VPCE ENI ranges -> caused intermittent 5xx as endpoints rotated.

ken-customer: ok thanks. one more: is there any code workaround on our side if our clients can't be updated right away?

sasha-eng: short-term workaround: use curl/SDK option to set Host header explicitly or use --resolve to hit the endpoint IP with proper Host. Example SDK change: set base URL to https://api.redwood.internal and ensure Host header is included in requests. Alternatively, configure the NLB to terminate TLS (listener TLS with cert) so backend doesn't depend on SNI. But TLS termination at NLB means cert management at LB level.

elaine-support: I'll send these repro steps to the customer and advise them to whitelist VPCE ENI ranges and verify that their in-VPC appliances (proxy/inspector) are not stripping SNI. If they confirm their SDKs are SNI-capable and still see failures, we'll open a deeper infra ticket to capture pcap on target and endpoint ENI.

deploy-bot: Deployment noticed —sidcar-proxy v2.3.1 rolled in staging 1766667800 (info only).

ken-customer: thanks everyone — will try Host header and whitelist the ENI ranges, will report back in this thread with results. :thumbsup:
